title: Learned image analysis identifies interstitial zirconium in alloyed ceria films
summary: A random-forest classifier trained on simulated electron-microscopy reconstructions helped distinguish isolated from overlapping zirconium interstitials in measured alloyed-ceria films. Author-deposited primary data describe octahedral interstitial zirconium at roughly 10²⁰ cm⁻³ and associated local disorder. The data were publicly released on October 22, before the November 16 journal article. A contribution to unusual electromechanical behavior remains a proposed interpretation.
ai_technology: Random forest classification of multislice electron-ptychography features
organization: Massachusetts Institute of Technology; Pennsylvania State University; Rice University

source_review.scope: Read original author-deposited Dryad Methods/README identifying the simulated training configurations, RF classifier, experimental assignment and represented structural findings, plus the exact publisher-deposited article abstract. Canonical article DOI/title and November16 date matched fresh Crossref metadata; October22 is the distinct primary data-release date. Full journal Methods and raw19.64GB dataset were not inspected.

evidence.tested: Depth-resolved electron-ptychography reconstructions of ceria and zirconium-alloyed films were compared with simulated known interstitial configurations. A 400-tree random forest used four integrated-potential/depth-width features to classify experimental interstitials as isolated, two- or three-atom overlaps, or weaker signals. The author deposit reports octahedral zirconium interstitials at approximately 10²⁰ cm⁻³ and associated lattice/oxygen-vacancy disorder.
evidence.unknown: Experimental atom assignments depend on the reconstruction and simulated reference configurations. Classifier validation described in the deposit uses held-out simulations, not independently established atom-by-atom experimental labels. The final article Methods, full raw dataset and all classifier uncertainty figures were not reviewed. A causal explanation of giant electrostriction or a general defect mechanism is not established by this entry.
evidence.ai_role: The RF learned simulation-derived signatures of isolated and overlapping interstitial atoms and assigned corresponding classes to experimental reconstruction features, enabling the represented interstitial interpretation.
